name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm test -- --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json="$RUNNER_TEMP/vitest.json"
      - name: Slowest test files
        env:
          REPORT: ${{ runner.temp }}/vitest.json
        run: |
          node --input-type=module <<'EOF'
          import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
          const limit = 10;
          const root = process.cwd().replaceAll("\\", "/") + "/";
          const files = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.env.REPORT, "utf8")).testResults
            .map(f => ({ file: f.name.replace(root, ""), seconds: (f.endTime - f.startTime) / 1000 }))
            .sort((a, b) => b.seconds - a.seconds);
          console.log("Slowest 10 test files:");
          for (const f of files.slice(0, 10)) console.log(`${f.seconds.toFixed(2).padStart(7)} s  ${f.file}`);
          const slow = files.filter(f => f.seconds > limit);
          for (const f of slow) console.log(`::error file=${f.file}::${f.file} took ${f.seconds.toFixed(1)} s; a test file may take at most ${limit} s. Split it, or mock the slow part (AGENTS.md Tests).`);
          if (slow.length) process.exit(1);
          EOF
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run check:bundle

  database:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Start the test backend
        run: |
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
            npm run setup -- --qa && exit 0
            echo "::warning::Starting the test backend failed (attempt $attempt); the image registry limits pulls. Trying again."
            sleep $((attempt * 30))
          done
          exit 1
      - run: npm run test:db

  browser:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    env:
      E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Start the test backend
        run: |
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
            npm run setup -- --qa && exit 0
            echo "::warning::Starting the test backend failed (attempt $attempt); the image registry limits pulls. Trying again."
            sleep $((attempt * 30))
          done
          exit 1
      - run: npm run qa:auth
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Browser journeys
        run: npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1 --retries=1 e2e/net-worth.gated.spec.ts e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts
      - name: Upload failure traces and screenshots
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: browser-failures
          path: test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore
name: Desktop

# Builds Moneo Desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux, smoke-tests the packaged app, and on a `v*` tag
# drafts a GitHub release with the installers. Packages are unsigned unless the signing secrets exist.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "scripts/desktop/**"
      - "next.config.ts"
      - "package*.json"
      - "supabase/migrations/**"
      - ".github/workflows/desktop.yml"
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: desktop-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: ${{ matrix.id }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { id: win-x64, runner: windows-latest, builder: "--win --x64" }
          - { id: mac-arm64, runner: macos-15, builder: "--mac --arm64" }
          # macos-13 was retired; macos-15-intel is the remaining Intel runner, so mac-x64 builds
          # and is smoke-tested natively.
          - { id: mac-x64, runner: macos-15-intel, builder: "--mac --x64" }
          - { id: linux-x64, runner: ubuntu-24.04, builder: "--linux --x64" }
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check release version
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      # No setup-go: fetch-backend.mjs downloads its own pinned Go toolchain into desktop/.cache.
      - run: npm ci

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: desktop/.cache
          key: desktop-cache-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs') }}

      - name: Fetch the native backend
        run: node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform ${{ matrix.id }}

      - run: npm run desktop:build

      - name: Package
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          WIN_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_LINK }}
          WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # electron-builder skips signing on pull requests; sign (ad hoc without a certificate) so
          # codesign's checks fail here instead of first on a release tag.
          CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST: "true"
        run: |
          # Secrets that do not exist arrive as empty strings; unset them so electron-builder
          # treats the build as unsigned.
          for name in CSC_LINK CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID WIN_CSC_LINK WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then unset "$name"; fi
          done
          if [ -z "${CSC_LINK:-}" ] && [ -z "${WIN_CSC_LINK:-}" ]; then
            export CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false
            echo "No signing certificate: building unsigned packages."
          fi
          npm run desktop:dist -- ${{ matrix.builder }} --publish never
          # Both Mac jobs write latest-mac.yml. Macs only read the version from it (unsigned apps
          # download from the release page), so the Apple Silicon one is kept.
          if [ "${{ matrix.id }}" = "mac-x64" ]; then rm -f desktop/release/latest-mac.yml; fi

      - name: List packages
        run: ls -la desktop/release

      # The smoke test starts the unpacked app (own temporary home, no cloud calls).
      - name: Linux dependencies for the smoke test
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libnss3-tools
          # Ubuntu 24.04 blocks the unprivileged user namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs.
          sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          mkdir -p smoke
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1280x1024x24" npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          else
            npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          fi

      - name: Upload installers
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: moneo-desktop-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: |
            desktop/release/*.exe
            desktop/release/*.dmg
            desktop/release/*.zip
            desktop/release/*.AppImage
            desktop/release/*.deb
            desktop/release/*.blockmap
            desktop/release/latest*.yml
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload smoke logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: smoke-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: smoke/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 3

  release:
    name: Draft release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: moneo-desktop-*
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Draft the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version."
            exit 1
          fi
          cd installers
          ls -la
          files=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.exe' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.AppImage' -o -name '*.deb' -o -name '*.blockmap' -o -name 'latest*.yml' \) -printf '%f\n' | sort)
          if [ -z "$files" ]; then echo "::error::No installers were downloaded."; exit 1; fi
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          sha256sum $files > SHA256SUMS.txt
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft --verify-tag \
            --title "Moneo Desktop $TAG" \
            --notes "Moneo Desktop $TAG. Packages are unsigned unless noted; check SHA256SUMS.txt." \
            $files SHA256SUMS.txt

1	# Making OpenClaw CI faster and 95% cheaper · Vincent Koc
2	
3	https://vincent.build/openclaw-ci-cost-reduction/
4	
5	!ci-article-artwork-v2.png
6	
7	When I first talked about the dark factory—agents building software with other agents—people laughed. More people are now using agents this way. Ours ran into a different limit: not tokens, memory or disk, but tests.
8	
9	Agents were producing code faster. They were also producing more tests, more jobs and more retries. Work piled up while we waited for checks to show that changes were safe to ship. We had a hard deadline to reduce how much compute we needed.
10	
11	About **89% of our code is TypeScript**.1 That is where I began with faster tools and adaptive testing. The broader lessons—remove weak tests, balance work and stop repeating setup—apply across languages.
12	
13	Our Blacksmith runners logged **158,546 hours** in the September peak week and **21,395 hours** in the latest week: **86.5% less runtime**. The estimated value of that compute fell **95.5%**. Blacksmith sponsored the capacity—we did not pay those dollar amounts. The workload also changed, so neither reduction belongs to one fix. Here is what we changed: fewer pointless checks, better use of each machine and tests that adapt.
14	
15	### Try this with your agent
16	
17	Short on time? Send your agent this page and the OpenClaw CI implementation, then give it this prompt:
18	
19	```
20	Read https://vincent.build/openclaw-ci-cost-reduction/ and its linked OpenClaw CI implementation. Audit this repository’s CI and measure a baseline. Propose the highest-value changes, then implement them in reviewable steps. Preserve required checks; run the full suite when affected-test selection is uncertain. Verify correctness, feedback time and compute cost. Don’t assume OpenClaw’s tools or results transfer unchanged.
21	```
22	
23	## Who runs the tests, and what we measured
24	
25	GitHub Actions coordinates the work: which jobs run, their dependencies and their results. A runner is the machine doing that work. We use Blacksmith (and more recently, boat.dev) to supply those runners on top of GitHub Actions.
26

51

A workflow can fan out into many jobs. That count covers one workflow in one repository; the Blacksmith totals above cover all repositories on the account.

55	
56	Activity fell too: indexed commits in the main repository were about **44% lower** across the comparison weeks (3,850 → 2,149). That is one repository against organization-wide cost, with slightly different daily boundaries, so it is context—not a saving measured at equal activity levels. Counting method.
57	
58	At Blacksmith’s published prices, keeping up the September week’s usage for 30 days would mean **$1.27 million worth of compute**. At the latest week’s usage, it would be **$57,324**2.
59	
60	A faster runner is useful, but it cannot fix poorly divided work. If each job spends most of its time preparing to run, buying faster execution tackles the smaller part of the problem. Our next step was to look at what we were asking those machines to do.
61	
62	The workload changed over this period too. The chart measures the combined result, not a saving we can assign to each fix. We also need to know how quickly changes get checked, reviewed and merged.
63	
64	The methods below are not tied to Blacksmith. We used its runners, but removing duplicate work, choosing relevant tests, reusing setup and balancing jobs apply to hosted runners and machines you operate yourself. The TypeScript examples show where we started, not where the ideas stop.
65	
66	## The goal: finish changes sooner
67	
68	I call this measure **agent cycle time: PR creation to merge**. It measures elapsed time for work done with agents, not every aspect of software quality.
69	
70	Writing the patch is only part of that interval. A PR can wait for a runner, install the same dependencies again, run an oversized suite, fail, get fixed and repeat. Review adds another wait. If another agent needs that change, that agent has to wait too.
71	
72	We have one objective: **finish useful work sooner, with less compute wasted along the way**. The first question is whether the work needs to run at all. Only then should we optimize the work that remains. A cheaper machine is not a win if it makes every dependent agent wait much longer. A faster machine is not a win if most of it sits idle.
73	
74	Removing unnecessary work can improve both. The job that never needed to start costs nothing and holds nobody up.

98	
99	## 1. Delete the waste before optimizing it
100	
101	A test is useful when it catches a mistake we care about. More test code is not automatically more protection. My starting assumption in an agent-grown suite is that most tiny, implementation-mirroring unit tests are noise until they can demonstrate an independent contract. By noise I mean tests that restate the implementation, fail during harmless refactors, or stay green when the behavior they claim to protect is broken.
102	
103	Models are very good at adding code. My reading: adding a test looks thorough; deleting one means showing that nothing useful is lost. Ask for a fix and it is easy to get another fixture, another mock and five assertions for behavior another suite already proves. Deletion needs an explicit instruction and a place in the definition of done. Otherwise the suite keeps growing even when the product barely changes.
104	
105	Make every test earn its place before buying it a faster machine. Speeding up noise leaves the maintenance problem intact.
106	
107	Our cleanup worked one subsystem at a time. Read the production code and its tests. Name the contract. Find the strongest test that proves it. Only then remove duplication—or repair a test that proves nothing.
108	
109	### Set a limit on test-code growth
110	
111	We put that pressure into a guard, not just a prompt. The original test-line ratchet told an over-budget change to **“Offset the added lines by deleting or consolidating tests elsewhere”**, or justify a higher ceiling. The rule was: once the suite is at its ceiling, further test lines must be offset by deletion or consolidation, or the ceiling must be raised with a stated justification. That was the 24 October guard. It is a limit on the amount of test code, not a reason to delete useful product code or the only regression test.
112	
113	The rule evolved. By the 13 November checkpoint, the per-change policy allows **400 net new test lines** without an allocation record; larger additions need a recorded, justified allowance. So it is not a blanket one-line-in, one-line-out rule. The principle survives: make growth visible, make exceptions explicit, and reward consolidation. Original guard · Versioned budget.
114

content.text:
I opened PR [#288](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/288). It should roughly halve the Desktop workflow, from about 25 minutes per pull request to about 12, once it's merged. Those numbers are estimates: no CI run has tested the changes yet.

**Where the time goes.** The `CI` workflow already finishes in about 3 minutes, so I left it alone. The slow one is `Desktop`, which took 20–34 minutes on each of the last 9 runs. The Intel Mac job is the slowest at about 28 minutes.

**Two causes, both fixed:**

1. **Each Mac job built the app twice.** `desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs` hardcoded both Mac chip types, which overrode the `--x64`/`--arm64` flag. So both Mac jobs packaged both apps, which accounts for about 10 minutes of packaging on Intel. This is also a release bug: the Intel job's Apple Silicon DMG had no Apple Silicon backend, and a release could ship it in place of the real one. Now the flag decides.
2. **The caches never worked.** A pull request can only reuse caches saved on its own branch or on `main`, and Desktop never ran on `main`. So every pull request downloaded the backend again (up to 5 minutes), then spent up to 3 minutes saving a 500 MB copy that nothing else could use. About 2 GB of these copies per pull request were also pushing other caches out of GitHub's 10 GB limit. A new job now fills the backend and npm caches on `main`: when the lock file or the fetch script changes, and once a week so they don't expire. Pull request runs only read them.

**Still to check:**
- The Desktop run on #288 will only show the packaging fix, because nothing on `main` has filled the caches yet.
- The new cache job only runs on `main`, so it can't be tested before merge. The first pull request after the merge will show whether the caches hit.
- I didn't run `npm test` or `npm run lint` locally. This checkout has no `node_modules`, and the changes are one config line and the workflow file. I only checked that the workflow file is valid YAML.

**Other ideas from the article:**
- **Worth doing later:** run the Intel Mac job only when `desktop/` or `scripts/desktop/` changes, not on every `package.json` or migration change. That's the article's "test the change" idea. Even after this PR, it's still the slowest job at about 12 minutes.
- **Not worth it here:** test selection, splitting tests across machines, and cleaning out weak tests pay off for huge test suites. Ours runs in about 30 seconds.
- **No gain:** splitting the `CI` checks into separate jobs wouldn't make the run finish sooner, because the browser job already takes about 3 minutes anyway.
